Also included a CSV of the switch port mapping for the three initial racks (switch-port-mapping.csv). Please mark any required changes inline.

Goal: have a validated demarc diagram and a runbook for cutover by next Friday (2029-07-19). Can Redwood provide a one‑pager of the control-plane endpoints and cert rotation expectations for the private deployment?

Appreciate the quick help — happy to hop on a 30m call if helpful.

Best,

Alice — thanks for the packet. I pulled the team in and attached a draft demarc diagram that overlays Redwood's control/data flows and recommended ACLs. Notes below and next steps.

Summary answers (short):
- Control plane: we will originate management connections from our control plane VIPs in 10.244.0.0/22 (mutual TLS). Data plane inference egress will use routable ranges you assign per-site — we recommend unique /24s per site for NAT clarity.
- BGP/Fallback: we support an active/active primary with active/passive failover to the colo provider. We prefer local_pref steering for primary, and prepend on failover; communities: no-export for internal peering, and use community 65000:100 for Redwood-prefer if you need to steer.
- MTU: recommend 9000 (jumbo frames) across the path for large KV cache pulls; if your infra cannot support it, 1500 is acceptable with a note that large model downloads may fragment.

Follow-ups and open items:
1) Karthik — can you confirm the cert principals we publish for control plane mTLS and the certificate rotation cadence? I sketched placeholders in the attached diagram.
2) Marissa — we should draft the cutover runbook (preflight checks, traffic-shift validation, rollback steps). I can take the canary cutover checklist.
3) Alice — can you confirm the exact ASN(s) for the colo provider and whether they require MD5 auth for BGP sessions?

Proposed next touch: 30m validation call Thursday 2029-07-11 09:00 PT. If that works I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,

On Thu, 10 Jul 2029 at 11:05, Stephanie Nguyen wrote:
> Alice — thanks for the packet. I pulled the team in and attached a draft demarc diagram that overlays Redwood's control/data flows and recommended ACLs. Notes below and next steps.

Thanks — adding a few technical clarifications from the inference runtime side: 
- Control-plane principals: Redwood will present SANs: control.redwood.internal, control.us-west.redwood, and per-customer principals of the form acme-<site>-ctrl.redwood. Certificates rotate quarterly; we'll notify 14 days in advance and support a 7‑day overlapped validity window for cutover.
- Keepalive/Timers: we recommend 30s BGP keepalive / 90s hold for upstream peering; if your colo recommends faster timers for rapid failover we can match.
- Data-plane egress NATing: Redwood's data-plane nodes will prefer using a site-specific egress IP. For multi-tenant racks we will rely on VLAN isolation plus source NAT unless you want us to advertise tenant prefixes directly (more complex).
- Testing plan for failover: we propose two tests in preflight — 1) BGP withdraw one primary path and validate inference request percentiles do not exceed 2x latency baseline, 2) re-introduce path and validate KV cache warm-up time <= 120s.

I also flagged a small mismatch in the switch-port CSV: port 1/12 on Rack A seems labeled as OOB instead of data; please confirm — if that's correct we need a small patch to the wiring map.

I'll join the Thursday call and can demo a quick synthetic traffic test harness during the meeting.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
